outcome: Physiologic Labor Interventions (Intermittent Fetal Monitoring, Ambulation, Hydrotherapy)
cohort: 360 healthy, nulliparous, obese (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) women with spontaneous labor onset at one hospital between 2005 and 2012.
finding: Obese women cared for by CNMs were significantly less likely to have operative vaginal birth and third- or fourth-degree perineal lacerations compared to those cared for by obstetricians, while other outcomes were similar.
